description: Team AstroByte is developing an AI-powered, web-based health monitoring solution for astronauts. Our team combines software development, AI, research, data analysis, design, and communication to support safer and healthier long-duration space missions.
summary: AstroByte Health Monitor is a web application that helps astronaut crews and reviewers track health changes and document follow-up actions during long-duration missions. In the public demo, users enter simulated observations or choose a scenario preset. Rule-based alerts show which readings triggered a flag and why. Reviewers can compare historical ISS radiation measurements from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) RadLab and attach that environmental reference to a follow-up note. By keeping the reading, alert explanation, and review note together, AstroByte demonstrates how crews could make health concerns easier to review and hand over between shifts.
details:
Crew health workflow

AstroByte brings health observations, alert explanations, and follow-up notes into one review workflow. In the public demo, select Multi-signal and Save observation to see how the system reviews simulated heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, sleep duration, and fatigue. Each alert shows the relevant reading and the illustrative range that triggered the rule. The combined alert groups multiple findings from the same observation so a reviewer can see what warrants a follow-up.

How we used NASA data

The demo includes a labeled snapshot of 180 historical absorbed dose-rate measurements from the ISS DosTel1 and DosTel2 instruments, obtained through NASA OSDR RadLab for a window on 1–2 April 2022 UTC. Reviewers can compare the two detectors, inspect the source and time window, and attach the radiation reference to a follow-up note. The alert rules evaluate crew observations. The historical radiation measurements provide environmental context during review.

Implementation

We built the interface with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The full workspace uses Node.js and SQLite for role-based access and persistent records. It supports observation history, trend views, and shift handovers. The public demo runs without an account or API key and can export the current session as JSON.

SI use

OpenAI Codex assisted with code, interface design, tests, documentation, and demo scripting. The full workspace includes an optional OpenAI integration that can prioritize findings already produced by local rules for synthetic observations. The public demo and default handover use deterministic rules.
Muse AI was used to generate selected visuals and animations in the project demonstration video.

Next steps

We plan to test wearable sensor integration and work with mission medical experts to validate the alert rules. The current thresholds are illustrative and require validation before operational use.
